for: Selection on survival alone raised skill at the selected task. With no reward for ability, SOLO gained +10.8 near-transfer energy against +2.6 under chance, and was above DRIFT in 5 of 5 seeds (paired gap +8.2, t 3.78). The gap is inside the pre-set noise band of 14.5, so the pre-set verdict stays as it is. The paired check was added after seeing the data.
Selection removed harmful instincts. 40% of generation 0 agents held a harmful rule. The final share was 41% under chance and 6% in SOLO, 8% in MEDLEY, 9% in CULTURE.

Punishment held grabbing down, as Theory 3 requires. Over all generations the grab rate was 7.8% in ALPHA with no vote, 1.9% in DOMEST and 0.6% in MEDLEY. In seed 4 the rule "Take the whole harvest whenever you can." spread from 19% to 94% of ALPHA agents and grabbing reached 71%. In DOMEST, from the same start, the rule was gone by generation 4, after an exile in generation 3.

Inherited notes carried usable knowledge, as Theory 4 requires. Final CULTURE populations earned +3.1 near-transfer energy with their notes compared with the same agents without them, higher in 5 of 5 seeds. In MEDLEY the figure was +3.0, higher in 4 of 5.
against: General ability did not move in any arm. Changes ran from -0.002 to +0.029 against +0.014 under chance and a noise band of 0.085. This is the test the thesis depends on.

No evolved population beat the model with no evolved text. Final general ability was 0.490 to 0.520 across arms and the bare model scored 0.554. On code-breaking every arm ended below the bare model, the closest by 0.059.
No theory arm beat plain ecology. SOLO gained +10.8 near-transfer energy. The best theory arm, CULTURE, gained +7.6, and 4 of 4 theory arms were below SOLO. MEDLEY was below SOLO in 5 of 5 seeds.
Less grabbing did not become more ability. DOMEST had the lowest rule-induction change of any arm, -0.058, inside the noise band of 0.105.

The two hidden laws were not found and passed on. At most 5% of any final population has text matching law 1. The matches for law 2 are fixed orders invented by the mutation writer, for example "Always soak first, then pound, and roast last; drying can wait." They appear under chance alone too, in 11% of final DRIFT agents.
Notes did not help outside their own world. With notes, MEDLEY's general ability was -0.027 relative to the same agents without them, lower in 5 of 5 seeds. In CULTURE the figure was -0.013.
untested: Whether selection can lift ability above the starting model. The weights never changed, and generation 0 began below the bare model (20.9 against 29.6 near-transfer energy) because the starting pool includes harmful rules. Every gain here is recovery toward the bare model.

Theory 3 at full strength. Exile removed 4 members in 120 generations, and grabbing took off in only one ALPHA seed, so the contrast between ALPHA and DOMEST rests on that seed. In MEDLEY seed 1 the grab rule reached 100% of agents while grabbing stayed at 3%, so holding the rule did not always produce grabbing.

A fair near test for the paired arms. The near test is a solo season, the activity SOLO and CULTURE were selected on. Advising, sharing and voting were selected in the paired arms and no test scores them.
Longer runs and larger groups. 12 generations of 16 agents over 5 seeds gave a chance spread of 14.5 energy, wider than any effect seen.

notes.mention_caveat: Shares are recomputed from the stored text with the corrected keyword check. The matches for L2 are fixed orders invented by the mutation writer that happen to end with dry. None states the law.
limits: Rules are cut at 14 words, so some rules written by the mutation writer end mid-sentence.
The paired per-seed comparison was added after seeing the data. It is more sensitive than the pre-set rule and is reported next to it. The verdicts use the pre-set rule only.
In the measurement, 62 of 28,825 calls returned nothing and 44 replies could not be parsed. Each counted as a failed try.
